newsitem.title: FRANCE: French finance minister against "Big Mac tax".
newsitem.headline: French finance minister against "Big Mac tax".

text.p: French Finance Minister Jean Arthuis has said he does not favour an increase in the tax on fast food, dubbed the "Big Mac tax", proposed by parliament's finance committee, Le Parisien newspaper reported on Tuesday.
The Finance Ministry confirmed Arthuis had told the daily: "My aim is to bring down Value Added Tax (VAT) for traditional restaurants...rather than to increase the tax on take-aways."

The finance committee last week adopted an amendment to the 1997 budget bill almost quadrupling the rate of VAT on takeout food from 5.5 to 20.6 percent. The government has the power to override amendments.

Nicknamed the "Big Mac tax" because it would hit U.S. hamburger giant McDonalds Corp, the amendment followed pressure from cafe and restaurant owners charging unfair competition because they have to pay the full rate of VAT on food and drink, while fast-food outlets pay the lower rate charged on retail food.

Fast-food companies hit back on Tuesday with newspaper advertisements to urge members of parliament not to penalise the young. It said 65 percent of its customers were aged under 25 and fast-food chains were big employers of young people.

"Raising VAT to 20.6 percent on take-away sales is deliberately plunging a young, popular and job-creating sector into crisis. Members of Parliament, listen to your children," The National Fast Food Association (SNARR) said in the adverts.
